takeaways: Copilot, Fabric and Azure AI (now Microsoft Foundry) are three stacked layers of one Microsoft stack, not competing products.
Copilot only surfaces what a user can already access, so cleaning up overshared permissions and training people matter more than buying licenses.
Start with Copilot where your work already happens, add Fabric if you live in reports and data, and turn to Foundry only when you need to build custom AI tools or agents.
hook: Azure AI, Copilot and Fabric AI sound like rivals, and Microsoft's constant renaming makes it worse. This episode untangles the three for beginners and career changers, showing what each layer does, its honest limits and costs, and how they fit together. You'll know which one you'll actually touch first and where to start learning.
